entries.question: How do ability values from a monster and its items combine?
answer: A monster has one value per ability; repeating the line overwrites it.
Items are added from all 8 slots. Depending on the ability, item values either add up or only the highest counts; each command page says which.
Bless effects come on top for units that receive them, then up to four temporary battle effects.

entries.question: Which units get bless effects, and what does darkbless do?
answer: Holy units receive their player's bless effects, and so do units with darkbless above 0. Bless values are always added on top of the unit's own and its items'.
So darkbless lets a unit that isn't holy benefit from blesses.

entries.question: Can a monster have two power lines?
answer: Yes, and both apply. Each power N value line is its own entry; the same N twice keeps only the last value.
N 1 to 499 names a power directly; 0 is the newest newritpow, -1 the one before. N of 500 or more is ignored.

entries.question: With several promotion or transformtarg entries, which one is used?
answer: Both only work on rituals; on a monster they do nothing.
A ritual runs every entry, in the order written.

transformtarg turns the target into the ritual's addstring monster (one picked at random per cast if there are several). promotion's value caps the number of units promoted: -1 promotes one, N up to N.

entries.question: How do inanimate and undead interact with banishment?
answer: Inanimate doesn't matter. Undead and demonic monsters can be banished, judged from the monster itself, not its items.
Undead can't be banished in Hades, demons not in Inferno.
Banishment destroys the unit; with banishsurv it is sent to another plane instead.

entries.question: How are the planes numbered?
answer: 0 Elysium, 1 Celestial Plane, 2 Sky, 3 Agartha, 4 Inferno, 5 Hades, 6 Aztlan, 7 Primal Plane, 8 Elemental Planes.
In events, -1 means any plane and -2 means Elysium, Sky or Agartha.

entries.question: Can a ritual give resources?
answer: Yes, with a negative cost: cost 0 -100 gives the caster 100 gold per cast. Works for resource types 0 to 13; type 15 gives random gems. Rebates shrink the gift like any cost.
gold, iron, herbs and similar lines inside a ritual are not costs: the cast stops with 'unknown ritual fx'.

entries.question: What happens when a repeated ritual runs out of resources?
answer: Each repetition is paid on its own, all or nothing. The first one that can't be paid ends the repeat and clears it; earlier casts are not refunded.
A mage repeats up to four times per turn, one action point each. Reaching maxcast also clears the repeat.

entries.question: In what order are event conditions checked?
answer: Top to bottom. The first failing condition ends the event; actions above it have already happened. There is no OR.
In a squareevent, square conditions (terrain, units here, owner) only drop that square; the rest (turn, season, variables, unit counts) end the event at once.
minunitshere is the exception: one square short of units ends the whole event. +hascom never passes in 5.42.

entries.question: How often do events run, and what happens on turn -1?
answer: Every event runs once per player per turn, squareevents included; add a player condition if it should fire once.
At game start, on turn -1, all events run once for each active player in slot order. turnnbr with no number is true only then. Loading a save skips this pass.

entries.question: What does the number on a newunits line do?
answer: It is the owner, not a count: 0 to 31 a player, -2 the event player, -3 the square's owner, -4 the army's owner.
Counts go in the string: "Name" one, "5*Name" five, "c*Name" a commander, "2d6*Name" dice, joined with " & ". Units after a c* group follow that commander.
Counts of three or more digits don't work: "100*Peasant" makes one Peasant.

entries.question: Do event actions run in order?
answer: Yes, line by line. A failed action never ends the event; only conditions do.

In a squareevent each action runs once per matching square. After a location command, every later line and repetition uses that one square, so randloc or scatterloc in a squareevent runs once per matching square, each from the previous result.

entries.question: What does randloc do if the terrain isn't on the map?
answer: It tries 500,000 random squares, then gives up and continues from the current square; the event goes on.
That search is slow, and in a squareevent it repeats for every matching square.
